1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 8 ) prescribes a method for the determination of total iron content in uncompounded natural rubber latex and uncompounded synthetic rubber latex which do not contain chlorine. 2. QUALITY OF REAGENTS and distilled water
impurities

2.1 Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals ( see IS : 1070-1977t ) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE - `Pure chemicals' shall which affect the result of analysis. mean chemicals

that do not contain

3. OUTLINE

OF THE

METHOD

3.1 Dried `latex solids are ashed in a crucible. The ash is extracted with hydrochloric acid and the solution is made up to standard volume. After adjustment of the PH by the addition of buffer solution, an aliquot part of the solution is treated with hydroxylammonium with which the iron forms a chloride and 1, - lo-phenanthroline The absorbance of this solution is measured coloured complex. photometrically, which is proportional to the concentration of iron. 4. 5.4 Buffer Solution - Dissolve 164 g of anhydrous sodium acetate in approximately 250 ml of water and to the solution add 28'5 ml of to 500 ml and glacial acetic acid ( sp gr 1'05 ). Dilute this mixture filter immediately before use if it is cloudy. If this buffer solution gives reference solutions in the preparation of the highly coloured calibration curve, an alternative buffer solution may be prepared by dissolving 80 g of sodium hydroxide or 106 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate in 200 ml of water, adding 142'5 ml of glacial acetic acid, (sp gr 1'05 ) and diluting the solution to 500 ml. 5.5 Standard Iron Solution (1 ml Contains 0'1 mg of Fe) Dissolve 0'702 1 g of ferrous ammonium sulphate hexahydrate [ (NHI)2Fe(S04),.6H,0] in water in a 1 OOO-ml volumetric flask. Add 3 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid ( sp gr 1'19 ) and dilute to This solution should remain stable for at least the mark with water. one month. 5.6 Standard Iron Working Solution (1 ml Contains 0'01 mg of Fe ) - Pipette 10 ml of the standard iron solution ( 5.5 ) into a lOO-ml This solution volumetric flask and dilute to the mark with water. shall be freshly prepared from the stock solution (5.5) when required. 6. PROCEDURE 6.1 Preparation of Test Portion latex, take a portion of thoroughly

IS : 9316 ( Part 8 ) - 1987 of total solids and dry to constant mass [set IS : 9316 ( Part 4 )-1979* 1. Homogenize the rubber so obtained by passing it a few times between the cold rolls of a laboratory mill to produce a thin sheet.
NOTE -At all stages of sample preparation, care shall be taken to avoid contamination with iron, particularly from rusty knives, scissors, mills, and other equipment.

6.2 Preparation of Calibration CurveMake up a series of standard matching solutions in 50-ml volumetric flasks, each containing 1 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid, 10 ml of buffer solution (5.4) 1 ml of hydroxylammonium chloride solution ( 5.3) and 10 ml of 1, lo-phenanthroline solution ( 5.2 ). To these solutions, add portions of the standard iron working solution (5.6), ranging from 0 to 20 ml ( for example 0; 0'5; 5; 10; 15; 20 ml ) and dilute the solutions with ,water to the mark. Allow to stand for 15 min, then decant each solution into the cell of the electrophotometer or spectrophotometer and measure its Correct the absorbance at the absorption maximum ( about 510 nm). reading by subtracting the absorbance of the solution containing no added iron. If the absorbance is measured on a double-beam instrument, place the cell containing the blank solution in the reference beam and measure the absorbance of each standard matching solution against that of the solution containing no added iron. Plot the reading thus obtained for each solution against the appropriate concentration of iron to give the calibration curve, which shall be checked periodically according to local conditions and the type of instrument used. 6.3 Determination

6.3.1 Cut a 10 g test portion of the dried latex into small pieces. Transfer to the unetched crucible and weigh to the nearest 0'01 g. Support the crucible in the hole cut in the asbestos board. Heat gently with a small gas flame until a dry carbonaceous residue remains and then transfer the crucible to the muffle furnace maintained at a temperature of 525 & 25�C. 6.3.2 Alternatively, wrap the weighed sample in a piece of ashless filter paper about 150 mm in diameter and transfer to the crucible. Place the crucible and its contents into the furnace at 525 f 25'C and The furnace door shall not be opened during close the furnace door. When the first hour because of the risk of igniting inflammable gases. all the carbon has been oxidized remove the crucible and allow to cool.
*Methods of test for rubber latex: Part 4 Determination of total solids content.

6.3.3 In parallel with the determination and following the same procedure, carry out a blank determination using similar filter paper and crucible and using the same quantities of all the reagents as used for the determination.
6.3.4 Add 5 ml of hydrochloric acid and 5 ml of water to the If crucible and digest the mixture on a steam bath for 30 to 60 min. the solution has a deep yellow colour, indicating the presence of much add a further 5 ml of the hydrochloric acid and digest for a iron, further 30 min. Filter the solution through a sintered glass crucible Collect the filtrate in a 50-ml volumetric (porosity grade 2 or 3 ). flask and dilute to the mark. 6.3.5 Transfer an aliquot part of this solution containing not more Add 10 ml `than 2 ml of hydrochloric acid to a 50-ml volumetric flask. of the buffer solution, then 1 ml of hydroxylammonium chloride Dilute to the solution and 10 ml of 1, lo-phenanthroline solution. mark with water and allow to stand at room temperature for 15 min. 6.3.6 Measure the absorbance of the solution at the wavelength used Correct the reading for the test for preparing the calibration curve. solution by subtracting the value for the absorbance o&the blank solutions. If the absorbance is measured on a double-beam instrument, place the cell containing the blank solution in the reference beam and measure the absorbance of the test solution against the blank solution.
NOTI.: - All precautions and saft,guards required for the carrying metal analysis shall be observed. out of trace

7. EXPRESSION

OF RESULTS

7.1 By means of the calibration curve, determine the concentration of iron corresponding to the corrected reading, and from this calculate Express the result as parts per the iron content of the test portion. million ( ppm ) of iron ( Fe ) calculated by mass.
